claim: Hepatocytes comprise 80% of the liver's volume.
source: Hepatocytes are the main cell type of the liver, comprising 80% of its volume and performing a vast array of vital functions including lipid metabolism, storage of macronutrients, secretion of plasma proteins, and xenobiotic detoxification (Gordillo et al., 2015; Si-Tayeb et al., 2010; Trefts et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Gordillo et al., 2015; Si-Tayeb et al., 2010; Trefts et al., 2017).

claim: Hepatocytes perform vital functions including lipid metabolism, storage of macronutrients, secretion of plasma proteins, and xenobiotic detoxification.
source: Hepatocytes are the main cell type of the liver, comprising 80% of its volume and performing a vast array of vital functions including lipid metabolism, storage of macronutrients, secretion of plasma proteins, and xenobiotic detoxification (Gordillo et al., 2015; Si-Tayeb et al., 2010; Trefts et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Gordillo et al., 2015; Si-Tayeb et al., 2010; Trefts et al., 2017).

claim: End-stage liver diseases require liver transplantation.
source: Diseases affecting these functions are life-threatening and end-stage forms require liver transplantation.
evidence: This is based on established medical knowledge about liver disease treatment.

claim: Only a limited number of patients can benefit from liver transplantation due to scarcity of donors and side effects of immunosuppression.
source: However, only a limited number of patients can benefit from this therapy due to scarcity of donors and the side effects of immunosuppression.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about limitations of organ transplantation.

claim: Cell-based therapy using primary hepatocytes is an attractive therapeutic alternative to whole organ transplants.
source: Cell-based therapy using primary hepatocytes has already been found to be an attractive therapeutic alternative to whole organ transplants (Dhawan et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Dhawan et al., 2020).

claim: Primary human hepatocytes are in short supply as they can only be obtained from suboptimal livers unsuitable for transplantation.
source: However, primary human hepatocytes (PHHs) are in short supply as they can only be obtained from suboptimal livers unsuitable for transplantation.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the source of primary hepatocytes.

claim: Primary human hepatocytes display a short life, absence of proliferation, and rapid loss of functionality in vitro.
source: Furthermore, they display a short life, absence of proliferation, and rapid loss of functionality in vitro (Mitry et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Mitry et al., 2002).

claim: Producing hepatocytes from human pluripotent stem cells using directed differentiation protocols is an advantageous alternative to primary human hepatocytes.
source: Producing hepatocytes from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) using directed differentiation protocols has been shown to be an advantageous alternative to PHHs (Palakkan et al., 2017; Szkolnicka and Hay, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Palakkan et al., 2017; Szkolnicka and Hay, 2016).

claim: Directed differentiation protocols commonly follow key stages of liver development in vitro.
source: These protocols commonly follow key stages of liver development in vitro and allow the production of hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs) which exhibit key hepatic functions including Albumin secretion, lipid metabolism, glycogen storage, and urea cycle activity.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about directed differentiation protocols.

claim: Hepatocyte-like cells exhibit key hepatic functions including Albumin secretion, lipid metabolism, glycogen storage, and urea cycle activity.
source: These protocols commonly follow key stages of liver development in vitro and allow the production of hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs) which exhibit key hepatic functions including Albumin secretion, lipid metabolism, glycogen storage, and urea cycle activity.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about HLC functionality.

claim: Hepatocyte-like cells systematically present an immature/foetal-like phenotype lacking the full repertoire of functions of mature hepatocytes.
source: However, HLCs systematically present an immature/foetal-like phenotype lacking the full repertoire of functions of mature hepatocytes (Baxter et al., 2015; Grandy et al., 2019; Yiangou et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Baxter et al., 2015; Grandy et al., 2019; Yiangou et al., 2018).

claim: Maturation is a process that occurs progressively in hepatocytes.
source: Maturation is a process that occurs progressively , and mimicking this timeline and the associated combination of metabolic changes, exposure to oxygen, nutrition, and microbiome constitutes a major challenge for direct differentiation protocols (Chen et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Chen et al., 2011).

claim: Overexpression of transcription factors has been explored as a way to improve functionality of in vitro generated hepatocytes.
source: As an alternative, overexpression of transcription factors (TFs) has been explored as a way to improve functionality of in vitro generated hepatocytes (Boon et al., 2020; Nakamori et al., 2016; Zhao et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Boon et al., 2020; Nakamori et al., 2016; Zhao et al., 2013).

claim: Transdifferentiation of somatic cells into liver cells has been achieved by overexpression of liver-enriched transcription factors in mouse and human fibroblasts.
source: Moreover, transdifferentiation of somatic cells into liver cells has been achieved by overexpression of liver-enriched transcription factors (LETFs) in mouse and human fibroblasts (Rombaut et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Rombaut et al., 2021).

claim: Liver-enriched transcription factors comprise the HNF1, HNF3 (FOXA), HNF4, and HNF6 (ONECUT) families.
source: Importantly, these LETFs comprise the HNF1, HNF3 (FOXA), HNF4, and HNF6 (ONECUT) families all of which play key roles in coordinating liver development (Gordillo et al., 2015; Lau et al., 2018; Schrem et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Gordillo et al., 2015; Lau et al., 2018; Schrem et al., 2002).

claim: HNF1, HNF3 (FOXA), HNF4, and HNF6 (ONECUT) families play key roles in coordinating liver development.
source: Importantly, these LETFs comprise the HNF1, HNF3 (FOXA), HNF4, and HNF6 (ONECUT) families all of which play key roles in coordinating liver development (Gordillo et al., 2015; Lau et al., 2018; Schrem et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Gordillo et al., 2015; Lau et al., 2018; Schrem et al., 2002).

claim: Direct cell conversion from somatic cell types has a low efficiency/yield due to strong epigenetic restrictions present in fully differentiated cells.
source: However, direct cell conversion from somatic cell types has a low efficiency/yield due to the strong epigenetic restrictions present in fully differentiated cells.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about cellular reprogramming.

claim: Somatic cells have restricted capacity of proliferation which limits large-scale production of hepatocytes without the use of oncogenic manipulation.
source: Furthermore, somatic cells have restricted capacity of proliferation which limits large-scale production of hepatocytes without the use of oncogenic manipulation (Du et al., 2014; Huang et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Du et al., 2014; Huang et al., 2014).

claim: The epigenetic state of human pluripotent stem cells is more permissive to direct cellular conversion than somatic cells.
source: Indeed, the epigenetic state of hPSCs is more permissive to direct cellular conversion, while their capacity of proliferation is far more superior to somatic cells.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the epigenetic state of pluripotent stem cells.

claim: The capacity of proliferation of human pluripotent stem cells is far more superior to somatic cells.
source: Indeed, the epigenetic state of hPSCs is more permissive to direct cellular conversion, while their capacity of proliferation is far more superior to somatic cells.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the proliferative capacity of pluripotent stem cells.

claim: Forward programming has been successfully used to generate neurons, skeletal myocytes, and oligodendrocytes using the OPTi-OX system.
source: Accordingly, this approach has been successfully used to generate neurons, skeletal myocytes, and oligodendrocytes by taking advantage of the OPTi-OX system (Pawlowski et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Pawlowski et al., 2017).

claim: Addition of doxycycline for 24 hr was sufficient to induce homogenous and robust expression of each liver-enriched transcription factor in human embryonic stem cells.
source: Addition of doxycycline (dox) for 24 hr was sufficient to induce homogenous and robust expression of each LETF in the selected human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) (Figure 1B and C) confirming the efficacy of the OPTi-OX system in inducing transgene expression.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Induction of liver-enriched transcription factors was not associated with differentiation into liver cells.
source: Importantly, this induction was not associated with differentiation into liver cells (data not shown) suggesting that LETFs alone are not sufficient to impose an hepatocytic identity.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations (data not shown).

claim: Liver-enriched transcription factors alone are not sufficient to impose a hepatocytic identity.
source: Importantly, this induction was not associated with differentiation into liver cells (data not shown) suggesting that LETFs alone are not sufficient to impose an hepatocytic identity.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that LETF induction did not cause differentiation.

claim: After 24 hr in E6 medium, cells acquired a hepatocyte-like morphology when cultured in Hepatozyme complete medium for 14 days.
source: Thus, we decided to screen culture conditions which could sustain both the survival and differentiation of hepatocytes (data not shown) and found that after the initial 24 hr in E6 medium, the cells acquired a hepatocyte-like morphology when cultured in Hepatozyme complete medium for 14 days (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Cells generated by overexpression of four liver-enriched transcription factors expressed hepatocyte markers such as Albumin, Alpha-1 Antitrypsin, and Alpha-Fetoprotein.
source: Interestingly, the resulting cells expressed hepatocyte markers such as Albumin (ALB), Alpha-1 Antitrypsin (A1AT or SERPINA1), and Alpha-Fetoprotein (AFP) (Figure 1E) and displayed CYP3A4 activity levels comparable to HLCs generated by direct differentiation, albeit several fold lower than PHHs (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Cells generated by overexpression of four liver-enriched transcription factors displayed CYP3A4 activity levels comparable to hepatocyte-like cells generated by direct differentiation.
source: Interestingly, the resulting cells expressed hepatocyte markers such as Albumin (ALB), Alpha-1 Antitrypsin (A1AT or SERPINA1), and Alpha-Fetoprotein (AFP) (Figure 1E) and displayed CYP3A4 activity levels comparable to HLCs generated by direct differentiation, albeit several fold lower than PHHs (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Cells generated by overexpression of four liver-enriched transcription factors displayed CYP3A4 activity levels several fold lower than primary human hepatocytes.
source: Interestingly, the resulting cells expressed hepatocyte markers such as Albumin (ALB), Alpha-1 Antitrypsin (A1AT or SERPINA1), and Alpha-Fetoprotein (AFP) (Figure 1E) and displayed CYP3A4 activity levels comparable to HLCs generated by direct differentiation, albeit several fold lower than PHHs (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: HNF1A, HNF6, or FOXA3 were necessary to generate cells expressing hepatocyte markers such as Albumin.
source: Induction of each combination of three LETFs in culture conditions identified above showed that HNF1A, HNF6, or FOXA3 were necessary to generate cells expressing hepatocytes markers such as ALB, albeit with heterogeneity at the protein level (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: HNF4A overexpression was dispensable for generating cells with hepatocyte characteristics.
source: HNF4A overexpression seemed to be dispensable as cells generated by overexpression of the three remaining LETFs (HNF1A, HNF6, FOXA3) acquired a cobblestone-like morphology, and expressed high levels of ALB, SERPINA1, and AFP (Figure 1G, H and I, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G, H, I and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cells generated by overexpression of HNF1A, HNF6, and FOXA3 acquired a cobblestone-like morphology.
source: HNF4A overexpression seemed to be dispensable as cells generated by overexpression of the three remaining LETFs (HNF1A, HNF6, FOXA3) acquired a cobblestone-like morphology, and expressed high levels of ALB, SERPINA1, and AFP (Figure 1G, H and I, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G, H, I and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cells generated by overexpression of HNF1A, HNF6, and FOXA3 expressed high levels of Albumin, SERPINA1, and Alpha-Fetoprotein.
source: HNF4A overexpression seemed to be dispensable as cells generated by overexpression of the three remaining LETFs (HNF1A, HNF6, FOXA3) acquired a cobblestone-like morphology, and expressed high levels of ALB, SERPINA1, and AFP (Figure 1G, H and I, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G, H, I and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Hepatocytes generated using three transcription factors (HNF1A, HNF6, FOXA3) achieved the highest levels of CYP3A4 activity.
source: Strikingly, hepatocytes generated using these 3TFs (3TF FoP-Heps) achieved the highest levels of CYP3A4 activity suggesting overexpression of HNF4A itself is unnecessary to acquire the hepatocyte characteristics screened, as its expression might be induced by one of the three LETFs (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Overexpression of HNF1A, HNF6, and FOXA3 is sufficient to forward program human pluripotent stem cells towards hepatocyte-like cells.
source: Altogether, these results showed that overexpression of HNF1A, HNF6, and FOXA3 is sufficient to forward program hPSCs towards HLCs.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results showing that these three factors can generate hepatocyte-like cells.

claim: Hepatocyte-like cells generated by direct differentiation represent a foetal state.
source: Despite displaying key hepatic functions (Baxter et al., 2015; Grandy et al., 2019; Yiangou et al., 2018), HLCs represent a 'foetal' state as shown by the expression of AFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,D) or by the limited activity/expression of CYP3A4, CYP2A6, or CYP2C9 (Figure 1B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,D,E and citations (Baxter et al., 2015; Grandy et al., 2019; Yiangou et al., 2018).

claim: Principal component analysis of the most variable 500 genes showed a clear distinction between hepatocyte-like cells, undifferentiated human induced pluripotent stem cells, and primary human hepatocytes.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) of the most variable 500 genes showed a clear distinction between the three cell types, with HLCs clustering in-between undifferentiated hiPSCs and PHHs confirming their intermediate state of differentiation (PC1: 52%, Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Hepatocyte-like cells cluster in-between undifferentiated human induced pluripotent stem cells and primary human hepatocytes, confirming their intermediate state of differentiation.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) of the most variable 500 genes showed a clear distinction between the three cell types, with HLCs clustering in-between undifferentiated hiPSCs and PHHs confirming their intermediate state of differentiation (PC1: 52%, Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Genes uniquely expressed in primary human hepatocytes were associated with adult liver functions such as response to xenobiotic and xenobiotic metabolism, inflammatory response, and complement activation.
source: Genes uniquely expressed in PHHs (cluster 1) were associated with adult liver functions such as response to xenobiotic and xenobiotic metabolism, inflammatory response, and complement activation (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Genes expressed in both hepatocyte-like cells and primary human hepatocytes were involved in liver development, fatty acid metabolism, or broad cellular functions.
source: Genes expressed in both HLCs and PHHs (Heps; cluster 3) were involved in liver development, fatty acid metabolism, or broad cellular functions (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: 36 transcription factors were highly expressed in primary human hepatocytes versus hepatocyte-like cells (p<0.05, log2 fold change >2).
source: We then decided to focus specifically on TFs using a previously curated list (Lambert et al., 2018; Figure 2G and H) and identified 36 TFs highly expressed in PHHs vs. HLCs (p<0.05, log2 fold change >2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G and H and citation (Lambert et al., 2018).

claim: Reactome pathway analysis grouped transcription factors highly expressed in primary human hepatocytes into two main pathways: the NFI family and a cohort of eight nuclear receptors.
source: Interestingly, reactome pathway analysis grouped these TFs into two main pathways: the NFI family and a cohort of eight nuclear receptors (Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Nuclear receptors are known to be involved in key liver functions including the metabolism of lipids and glucose, bile acid clearance, xenobiotic sensing, and regeneration.
source: Nuclear receptors are known to be involved in key liver functions including the metabolism of lipids and glucose, bile acid clearance, xenobiotic sensing, and regeneration (Rudraiah et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Rudraiah et al., 2016).

claim: The immature state of hepatocyte-like cells is associated with the absence of several nuclear receptors.
source: Taken together these observations show that the immature state of HLCs is associated with the absence of several nuclear receptors thereby suggesting that these factors could be necessary to drive functional maturation of hepatocytes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that nuclear receptors are absent in HLCs but present in PHHs.

claim: Nuclear receptors could be necessary to drive functional maturation of hepatocytes.
source: Taken together these observations show that the immature state of HLCs is associated with the absence of several nuclear receptors thereby suggesting that these factors could be necessary to drive functional maturation of hepatocytes.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the association between nuclear receptor absence and HLC immaturity.

claim: Principal component analyses showed a marked divergence between the epigenetic profile of hepatocyte-like cells and human induced pluripotent stem cells independently of the histone mark analysed.
source: As expected, PCAs showed a marked divergence between the epigenetic profile of HLCs and hiPSCs independently of the mark analysed (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Hepatocyte-like cells and primary human hepatocytes clustered in close proximity in principal component analysis, suggesting that these cell types share an important part of their epigenetic profile.
source: Interestingly, HLCs and PHHs clustered in close proximity suggesting that these cell types share an important part of their epigenetic profile despite their transcriptomic differences.
evidence: This is inferred from the PCA clustering pattern.

claim: The profiles of H3K27ac and H3K27me3 showed the highest variance between hepatocyte-like cells/primary human hepatocytes and human induced pluripotent stem cells.
source: The profiles of H3K27ac and H3K27me3 showed the highest variance between HLCs/PHHs and hiPSCs, confirming the importance of these marks for establishing cellular identity (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: H3K4me1 was absent at primary human hepatocyte-specific regions in hepatocyte-like cells and seems to be broadly replaced by spread of H3K27me3 deposition instead.
source: This analysis revealed that H3K4me1 was absent at 'PHH-specific' regions in HLCs and seems to be broadly replaced by spread of H3K27me3 deposition instead (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Discrete portions of regulatory regions lacked H3K27ac in genes downregulated in hepatocyte-like cells.
source: Interestingly, discrete portions of regulatory regions lacked H3K27ac in genes downregulated in HLCs (see for example CYP3A4 and UGT1A, Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A subset of genes involved in adult liver functions lack H3K4me1 priming as well as full H3K27ac deposition in hepatocyte-like cells.
source: Overall, these results suggested that a subset of genes involved in adult liver functions lack H3K4me1 priming as well as full H3K27ac deposition in HLCs.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: Regions lacking H3K27ac in hepatocyte-like cells appeared to display repressive marks such as H3K27me3.
source: These regions lacking H3K27ac in HLCs appeared to display repressive marks such as H3K27me3.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: Hepatocyte-like cells and primary human hepatocytes broadly share the same epigenetic identity when compared to human induced pluripotent stem cells.
source: Taken together these observations suggested that HLCs and PHHs broadly share the same epigenetic identity when compared to hiPSCs.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: The activation of a limited and specific set of regulatory regions is missing in hepatocyte-like cells, which could explain the absence of expression of adult liver genes and lack of functional maturation.
source: However, the activation of a limited and specific set of regulatory regions is missing in HLCs, which could explain the absence of expression of adult liver genes and lack of functional maturation.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the epigenetic differences observed.

claim: Motif enrichment analysis in primary human hepatocyte-specific regions marked by H3K27ac identified a significant enrichment for the androgen and estrogen response elements, as well as RORc motifs.
source: Interestingly, this analysis identified a significant enrichment for the androgen (AR) and estrogen (ERα) response elements, as well as RORc motifs (Figure 3D), which were among the top differentially expressed nuclear receptors in our transcriptomic analyses.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The expression of RORc, AR, and ERα was found to be upregulated specifically in the adult mouse liver.
source: Interestingly, the expression of these three nuclear receptors was found to be upregulated specifically in the adult liver (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: The nuclear receptors AR, ERα, and RORc could play a role in establishing or maintaining a transcriptional network characterising mature hepatocytes.
source: Altogether, these observations suggested that the nuclear receptors AR, ERα, and RORc could play a role in establishing or maintaining a transcriptional network characterising mature hepatocytes.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the motif enrichment and expression data.

claim: RORc overexpression resulted in a higher number of cells expressing Albumin.
source: RORc overexpression resulted in a higher number of cells expressing Albumin, which were still heterogeneous across the cell population, potentially representing different subpopulations of HLCs (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Cells with RORc overexpression secreted higher levels of Albumin.
source: Moreover, these cells also secreted higher levels of Albumin, although the mRNA expression of this marker was not significantly upregulated (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: CYP3A4 activity levels were significantly higher in cells generated in the presence of RORc, as compared with cells forward programmed with only three transcription factors.
source: Notably, CYP3A4 activity levels were significantly higher in cells generated in the presence of RORc, as compared with cells forward programmed with only 3TFs (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: β-estradiol treatment resulted in a three fold increase in CYP3A4 activity.
source: Interestingly, only β-estradiol treatment resulted in a three fold increase in CYP3A4 activity, whereas testosterone treatment significantly decreased CYP3A4 activity and desmosterol had no effect (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Testosterone treatment significantly decreased CYP3A4 activity.
source: Interestingly, only β-estradiol treatment resulted in a three fold increase in CYP3A4 activity, whereas testosterone treatment significantly decreased CYP3A4 activity and desmosterol had no effect (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Desmosterol treatment had no effect on CYP3A4 activity.
source: Interestingly, only β-estradiol treatment resulted in a three fold increase in CYP3A4 activity, whereas testosterone treatment significantly decreased CYP3A4 activity and desmosterol had no effect (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The presence of RORc significantly increased basal CYP3A4 activity in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived forward programmed hepatocytes.
source: In addition, the presence of RORc significantly increased basal CYP3A4 activity thereby confirming the positive effect of this factor on functional maturity of FoP-Heps (Figure 4—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2H.

claim: Overexpression of specific nuclear receptors was compatible with the generation of forward programmed hepatocytes.
source: Overall, these results showed that overexpression of specific nuclear receptors was compatible with the generation of FoP-hepatocytes.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results showing successful generation of FoP-Heps with nuclear receptor overexpression.

claim: Overexpression of RORc could improve the functionality of hepatocytes generated by overexpression of three liver-enriched transcription factors.
source: In particular, overexpression of RORc could improve the functionality of hepatocytes generated by overexpression of three LETFs confirming the role of this nuclear receptor in hepatocyte maturation.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results showing improved functionality with RORc overexpression.

claim: CYP3A4 activity was significantly higher in 4TF forward programmed hepatocytes after 20 days than those achieved by hepatocyte-like cells after 30 days of directed differentiation.
source: CYP3A4 activity was significantly higher in 4TF FoP-Heps forward programmed after 20 days than those achieved by HLCs after 30 days of directed differentiation (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Forward programmed hepatocytes expressed a range of functional markers confirming the acquisition of hepatic functionality.
source: FoP-Heps expressed a range of these functional markers confirming the acquisition of hepatic functionality (Figure 5B and C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B, C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The levels of expression achieved by forward programming were equivalent to those achieved by direct differentiation with the exception of gluconeogenesis genes which were increased in forward programmed hepatocytes.
source: Overall, the levels of expression achieved by forward programming were equivalent to those achieved by direct differentiation with the exception of gluconeogenesis genes which were increased in FoP-Heps (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Expression of gluconeogenesis and lipid metabolism genes was comparable between forward programmed hepatocytes and primary human hepatocytes.
source: Interestingly, expression of gluconeogenesis and lipid metabolism genes was comparable between FoP-Heps and PHHs.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data comparing gene expression levels.

claim: In forward programmed hepatocytes, the four transcription factors remained expressed at physiological levels at the end of the protocol.
source: Of note, in FoP-Heps, the 4TFs remained expressed at physiological levels at the end of our protocol (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The transcriptome of human embryonic stem cell-derived forward programmed hepatocytes closely clustered with hepatocyte-like cells derived from both human embryonic stem cells and human induced pluripotent stem cells.
source: As suggested by the marker expression pattern identified by qPCR, the transcriptome of eFoP-Heps closely clustered with HLCs derived from both hESCs and hiPSCs (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Both human embryonic stem cell-derived forward programmed hepatocytes and hepatocyte-like cells clustered separately from foetal liver cells.
source: Interestingly, both eFoP-Heps and HLCs clustered separately from foetal liver cells, indicating that despite these cells not acquiring a fully mature phenotype, these also don't fully resemble a foetal liver stage.
evidence: This is inferred from the clustering pattern in the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Genes that gain expression in human embryonic stem cell-derived forward programmed hepatocytes compared to undifferentiated human induced pluripotent stem cells are strongly associated with several liver functions such as hormone metabolism, lipid localisation and transport, blood coagulation.
source: As expected, genes that gain expression in eFoP-Heps compared to undifferentiated hiPSCs are strongly associated with several liver functions such as hormone metabolism, lipid localisation and transport, blood coagulation (Figure 5E), further confirming that cells generated by forward programming acquire a hepatocyte identity.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Human embryonic stem cell-derived forward programmed hepatocytes and human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived hepatocyte-like cells expressed a range of adult liver genes that were found to be highly expressed in adult primary human hepatocytes.
source: Indeed, eFoP-Heps, as well as hiPSC-derived HLCs, expressed a range of adult liver genes that were found to be highly expressed in adult PHHs as identified in Figure 2, Figure 2—source data 2, including genes that were not expressed in the foetal stage (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Both human embryonic stem cell-derived and human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived forward programmed hepatocytes were able to uptake low-density lipoprotein from the culture medium.
source: In addition to expressing mature hepatocyte markers, both eFoP-Heps and iFoP-Heps were also able to uptake low-density lipoprotein (LDL) from the culture medium confirming their capacity to transport lipids (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Forward programmed hepatocytes grown in 3D retained the expression of hepatocyte markers.
source: We first confirmed that FoP-Heps grown in 3D retained the expression of hepatocyte markers (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: SERPINA1 or UGT1A6 expression increased in forward programmed hepatocytes grown in 3D conditions.
source: Interestingly, SERPINA1 or UGT1A6 expression increased in these conditions suggesting an increase in functional maturation promoted by 3D (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Oleic acid treatment induced a strong accumulation of lipids in forward programmed hepatocytes.
source: In line with their known effect on hepatocytes, OA treatment induced a strong accumulation of lipids as shown by BODIPY staining (Figure 6C) while PA treatment induced a reduction in cell viability consistent with lipotoxicity (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Palmitic acid treatment induced a reduction in cell viability consistent with lipotoxicity in forward programmed hepatocytes.
source: In line with their known effect on hepatocytes, OA treatment induced a strong accumulation of lipids as shown by BODIPY staining (Figure 6C) while PA treatment induced a reduction in cell viability consistent with lipotoxicity (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Forward programmed hepatocytes react to fatty acids similarly to primary hepatocytes.
source: Thus, FoP-Heps appear to react to fatty acids similarly to their primary counterpart.
evidence: This is inferred from the observed responses to oleic acid and palmitic acid treatments.

claim: Acetaminophen treatment resulted in up to 50% reduction in cell viability of forward programmed hepatocytes.
source: This treatment resulted in up to 50% reduction in cell viability (Figure 6E) suggesting that FoP-Heps could be used for cytotoxic studies.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Forward programmed hepatocytes could be used for cytotoxic studies.
source: This treatment resulted in up to 50% reduction in cell viability (Figure 6E) suggesting that FoP-Heps could be used for cytotoxic studies.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observed response to acetaminophen.

claim: 4TF forward programmed hepatocytes derived from either human embryonic stem cells or human induced pluripotent stem cells display characteristics of functional hepatocytes.
source: In summary, these results showed that 4TF FoP-Heps derived from either hESC or hiPSCs display characteristics of functional hepatocytes such as expression of genes involved in drug, lipid, glucose and bile acid metabolism, capacity to uptake LDL and fatty acids from the culture medium, as well as response to hepatotoxic factors, demonstrating their potential interest for modelling liver disease in vitro and toxicology screening.
evidence: This is inferred from the comprehensive functional characterization performed.

claim: Production of hepatocytes by forward programming requires a more complex process involving three transcription factors and a culture media supporting primary hepatocytes.
source: Our results show that production of hepatocytes requires a more complex process involving three TFs but also a culture media supporting primary hepatocytes.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results showing the requirements for successful forward programming.

claim: The best liver-enriched transcription factor combination did not include HNF4A.
source: Furthermore, our best LETFs combination did not include HNF4A, which is known to be a key regulator of hepatocyte function in the adult liver.

source: Similar observations were recently reported for the direct reprogramming of human umbilical vein endothelial cells into bipotent hepatocyte progenitor cells where HNF4A was found to be detrimental (Inada et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Inada et al., 2020).

claim: HNF4A is essential in adult liver and during development, especially in the establishment of the liver bud.
